correctness.rationale: The positive stable cascade has a unique periodic state. The constant, fundamental and second harmonic of Q² are the only output components. Equal interior discharge pairs phases θ and −θ, so the response difference is 2 sin θ (B+2E cos θ). A simple root in cos θ implies a transverse crossing because the two branches have different derivatives in discharge there. For one or two positive rates the ratio of the second/fundamental imaginary transfer magnitudes is 2 times a product of factors less than 1, so |2E/B|<ε/q. For three equal rates the two imaginary-part zeros are distinct (x=3 and x=3/4), excluding a multiply traced curve, and the stated rational derivative gives the three monotonicity intervals of R with limits 1, infinity, 0 and 16. Threshold collisions are at extreme discharge, not interior double points. The full signed integral is −πεB. At x=3, B vanishes but the second sine coefficient does not, so integrating the branch separation on each side of Q=q gives the nonzero equal areas 12√3 ε³/2197 with opposite orientation. Independent Decimal bisection reproduces x₋=2.8734443468022209 and x₊=3.1358904359604235 for ε/q=1/2.
residual_risks: The frequency window assumes exactly three equal-rate stages. Only the lower-stage exclusion allows arbitrary positive unequal rates as stated.
No conclusions about transients or other source laws are supported.

originality.rationale: Figure-eight sediment loops, their opposite lobes and linear-cascade frequency responses are known. The supported distinction is the joint exact minimum stage count, bounded equal-rate frequency interval and area formula for a single positive sinusoid passed through the increasing quadratic source and serial first-order retention. The strongest distinct indexed overlap has a triangular event driver and two competing memories; it gives the geometry and net-area cancellation in a different family, not the two-stage impossibility or the serial transfer inequalities.

value.rationale: A known loop geometry is obtained from a single strictly increasing source by a proved minimal serial memory mechanism. The open bounded frequency interval separates robust crossings from isolated phase tuning. The nonzero lobe area at exactly zero net signed area gives a concrete benchmark for scalar hysteresis diagnostics. The result is useful as a reduced-model counterexample to identifying separate sources from loop shape alone, not as empirical attribution.
residual_risks: Sinusoidal periodic driver and idealized quadratic supply; no calibration to natural hydrographs or sediment concentrations.
